Plot a Bar Chart following WJP style guidelines

Source: R/barsChart.R
wjp_bars.Rd

wjp_bars() takes a data frame with long-format data and returns a ggplot object with a vertical or horizontal bar chart following WJP style guidelines. Values are expected on a 0-100 percentage scale.

Usage

wjp_bars(
  data,
  target,
  grouping,
  labels = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  cvec = NULL,
  direction = "vertical",
  stacked = FALSE,
  lab_pos = NULL,
  expand = FALSE,
  order = NULL,
  width = 0.9,
  ptheme = WJP_theme(),
  show_legend = FALSE,
  position = c("stack", "dodge"),
  dodge_width = NULL,
  series_reverse = FALSE,
  align = c("start", "center"),
  track = FALSE,
  track_color = "#E5E8E8",
  value_position = c("end", "outside", "center", "column"),
  value_offset = 5,
  value_size = 10,
  value_fontface = "bold",
  value_colors = NULL,
  limits = NULL,
  breaks = NULL,
  axis_labels = NULL,
  expand_mult = NULL,
  expand_discrete = NULL,
  value_axis = TRUE,
  grid = TRUE,
  grid_color = "#d1cfd1",
  ylab = "% of respondents",
  baseline = FALSE,
  baseline_color = "#1A1A1A",
  label_align = NULL,
  label_size = NULL,
  label_colour = NULL,
  label_wrap = NULL,
  label_lineheight = NULL,
  ref_lines = NULL,
  clip = "on",
  layout = NULL,
  legend_position = "top",
  legend_text_size = 11,
  legend_key_size = NULL,
  legend_fontface = "bold",
  legend_justification = "left"
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing the data to plot.

target

String. Column name of the variable that supplies the values to plot.

grouping

String. Column name of the variable that supplies the categories (X-axis for vertical bars, Y-axis for horizontal bars).

labels

String. Column name of the variable containing the value labels to display. Default is NULL (no labels).

colors

String. Column name of the variable that contains the color grouping (the series of stacked or side-by-side bars). Default is NULL (colors follow grouping).

cvec

Named vector of colors. Names should match the values of the colors variable. Default is NULL (the WJP palette, see wjp_palette(), is applied).

direction

String. Either "vertical" (default) or "horizontal".

stacked

Logical. Set to TRUE for stacked bars (several rows per category, one per segment) so value labels are drawn in white inside each segment. Default is FALSE.

lab_pos

String. Column name of the variable that contains the coordinates for the value labels. Default is NULL (labels follow value_position).

expand

Logical. If TRUE, the axis is expanded to give extra space for value labels above 100%. Default is FALSE.

order

String. Column name of the variable that contains the display order of categories. Default is NULL (data order).

width

Numeric value between 0 and 1. Width of bars as a fraction of the space available for each category. Default is 0.9.

ptheme

ggplot theme to apply. Default is WJP_theme().

show_legend

Logical. If TRUE, displays a horizontal legend above the chart using the colors values. This is most useful when colors differs from grouping, such as in stacked or side-by-side bars. Default is FALSE.

position

String. "stack" (default) stacks the rows of a category; "dodge" draws them side by side.

dodge_width

Numeric. Distance between the centers of side-by-side groups, as a fraction of the category space. Default is NULL (width).

series_reverse

Logical. Reverse the order of side-by-side series. Default is FALSE.

align

String. "start" (default, bars start at 0) or "center" (bars centered on the middle of the value axis).

track

Logical. Draw a 100% background track behind each bar. Default is FALSE.

track_color

String. Color of the track. Default is "#E5E8E8".

value_position

String. Position of the value labels: "end" (default), "outside", "center", or "column". See Details.

value_offset

Numeric. Distance, in points, between the end of a bar and its label when value_position = "outside". Default is 5.

value_size

Numeric. Size of the value labels, in points. Default is 10.

value_fontface

String. Font face of the value labels: "plain", "bold" (default), "italic", "bold.italic", or a weight face such as "semibold.italic" (see wjp_fonts()).

value_colors

Color of the value labels: one color, or a vector named by the colors values (one color per series). Default is NULL ("#4a4a49", white for stacked bars).

limits

Numeric vector of length 2 with the limits of the value axis. Use NA for a limit computed from the data (e.g., c(0, NA) scales the axis to the largest value). Default is NULL (c(0, 110), or larger with expand = TRUE).

breaks

Numeric vector with the breaks of the value axis. Default is NULL (every 20 points from 0 to 100).

axis_labels

Labels of the value-axis breaks: a character vector or a function. Default is NULL (percentages).

expand_mult

Numeric vector of length 1 or 2. Multiplicative expansion of the value axis. Default is NULL (ggplot2's default; none with a layout).

expand_discrete

Numeric of length 1 or 2. Space added before the first and after the last category (in reading order: top then bottom for horizontal charts, left then right for vertical ones), in categories. Default is NULL (0.6, or 0.5 with a layout).

value_axis

Logical. Show the labels of the value axis. Default is TRUE.

grid

Logical. Draw grid lines across the value axis. Default is TRUE.

grid_color

String. Color of the grid lines. Default is "#d1cfd1".

ylab

String. Title of the value axis (shown on vertical charts). Default is "% of respondents"; NULL removes it.

baseline

Logical. Draw a line at the start of the value axis. Default is FALSE.

baseline_color

String. Color of the baseline. Default is "#1A1A1A".

label_align

String. Alignment of the category labels: "left", "right", or "center". Default is NULL (left for horizontal charts, centered for vertical ones).

label_size

Numeric. Size of the category labels, in points. Default is NULL (the size of ptheme).

label_colour

String. Color of the category labels. Default is NULL (the color of ptheme).

label_wrap

Numeric. Maximum number of characters per line of the category labels. Default is NULL (no wrapping; existing line breaks are kept).

label_lineheight

Numeric. Line height of multi-line category labels. Default is NULL.

ref_lines

Reference lines: a numeric vector with positions on the category axis (in category units, e.g. 3.5 between the third and fourth categories), or a data frame with columns axis ("category" or "value"), position and, optionally, colour, linetype, and linewidth (points). Default is NULL.

clip

String. Whether to clip drawing to the panel: "on" (default) or "off" (keeps labels next to 100% visible).

layout

A wjp_layout() with the geometry of the chart in points. Default is NULL.

legend_position

Legend position: "top" (default), "bottom", "left", "right", or c(x, y) inside the panel.

legend_text_size

Numeric. Size of the legend text, in points. Default is 11.

legend_key_size

Numeric. Size of the legend keys, in points. Default is NULL.

legend_fontface

String. Font face of the legend text. Default is "bold".

legend_justification

String. Horizontal justification of a legend above or below the chart: "left" (default), "center", or "right".

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The function expects one row per bar: a category in grouping and its value in target. For stacked bars (stacked = TRUE), supply one row per segment (each grouping and colors combination) and precompute the label coordinates (lab_pos) at the center of each segment, or use value_position = "center"; segment labels are drawn in white.

Side-by-side series. With position = "dodge", rows that share a category are drawn next to each other (e.g., a country and the EU average), in the order of the colors values (factor levels or first appearance): the first series at the top of horizontal charts and at the left of vertical ones (series_reverse = TRUE swaps them). Value labels and the optional 100% track follow their bars.

Value labels. value_position = "end" (default) centers each label on the end of its bar, as in earlier versions, or on lab_pos when given. "outside" anchors it value_offset points after the end of the bar, and "center" puts it in the middle of the bar (or of its stacked segment), and "column" aligns the labels value_offset points after the 100% mark. Rows with a missing value draw their label at the start of the axis.

Centered bars. align = "center" centers every bar on the middle of the value axis (funnel-like layouts); see also wjp_funnel().

Geometry in points. With a wjp_layout(), horizontal charts keep a fixed label column (label_width, label_gap), a 100% track of track_width points followed by the value column (value_gap, value_width), a fixed row pitch (row_height) and bar height (bar_height), and margins. Vertical charts use row_height as the column pitch, bar_height as the column width, and track_width as the height of 100%. The category labels of horizontal charts are then drawn as a text layer in the label column.

Like all WJPr chart functions, the returned object is a regular ggplot, so further customizations can be layered with +.

Examples

library(dplyr)

# Always load the WJP fonts
wjp_fonts()

# Percentage of people that trust their institutions, by country
data4bars <- WJPr::gpp %>%
  filter(year == 2022) %>%
  mutate(
    q1a   = as.double(unclass(q1a)),
    trust = case_when(q1a <= 2 ~ 1, q1a <= 4 ~ 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(trust = mean(trust, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    value_label    = paste0(round(trust, 0), "%"),
    label_position = trust + 6
  )

# Vertical bars (default)
wjp_bars(
  data4bars,
  target   = "trust",
  grouping = "country",
  labels   = "value_label",
  lab_pos  = "label_position",
  cvec     = c("Atlantis"  = "#482d8b",
               "Narnia"    = "#2894aa",
               "Neverland" = "#f26b21")
)


# Horizontal bars
wjp_bars(
  data4bars,
  target    = "trust",
  grouping  = "country",
  labels    = "value_label",
  lab_pos   = "label_position",
  direction = "horizontal"
)


# Stacked bars: one row per segment, labels centered on each segment
data4stacked <- WJPr::gpp %>%
  filter(year == 2022) %>%
  mutate(
    q1a   = as.double(unclass(q1a)),
    level = case_when(q1a <= 2 ~ "Trust", q1a <= 4 ~ "No trust")
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(level)) %>%
  count(country, level) %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage     = n / sum(n) * 100,
    value_label    = paste0(round(percentage, 0), "%"),
    level          = factor(level, levels = c("No trust", "Trust")),
    label_position = if_else(
      level == "Trust", percentage / 2, 100 - percentage / 2
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

wjp_bars(
  data4stacked,
  target   = "percentage",
  grouping = "country",
  labels   = "value_label",
  lab_pos  = "label_position",
  colors   = "level",
  stacked  = TRUE,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  cvec     = c("Trust" = "#482d8b", "No trust" = "#f26b21")
)


# Country and EU average side by side, with a 100% track and values after
# each bar (fictional data)
paired <- data.frame(
  category = rep(c("Consumer", "Housing", "Employment"), 2),
  series   = rep(c("Atlantis", "EU Average"), each = 3),
  value    = c(40, 10, 19, 21, 7, 10)
)
paired$text <- paste0(paired$value, "%")

wjp_bars(
  paired,
  target         = "value",
  grouping       = "category",
  labels         = "text",
  colors         = "series",
  cvec           = c("Atlantis" = "#575796", "EU Average" = "#A8A8C8"),
  direction      = "horizontal",
  position       = "dodge",
  track          = TRUE,
  value_position = "outside",
  value_colors   = c("Atlantis" = "#575796", "EU Average" = "#7D7DA8"),
  value_axis     = FALSE,
  grid           = FALSE,
  label_align    = "right",
  show_legend    = TRUE,
  layout         = wjp_layout(label_width = 90, label_gap = 6,
                              track_width = 250, value_gap = 5,
                              value_width = 30, row_height = 21,
                              bar_height = 8)
)
